chapters.title: One Like a Son of Man
chapters.html:
Revelation 1

The Revelation of Jesus Christ

1The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants what must take place quickly. He made it known by sending it through His angel to His servant John,

2who testified to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus Christ, all that he saw.

3Blessed is the one who reads aloud, and blessed are those who hear the words of this prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.

To the Seven Churches

4John, to the seven churches in Asia: grace to you and peace from Him who is and who was and who is to come, and from the seven spirits who are before His throne,

5and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To Him who loves us and has freed us from our sins by His blood,

6and has made us a kingdom, priests to His God and Father, to Him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

7He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, even those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth will mourn over Him. Yes. Amen.

8"I am the Alpha and the Omega," says the Lord God, "who is and who was and who is to come, the Almighty."

The Vision on Patmos

9I, John, your brother and partner in the affliction and the kingdom and the endurance that are in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.

10I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like a trumpet,

11saying, "Write what you see in a book, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, to Smyrna, to Pergamum, to Thyatira, to Sardis, to Philadelphia and to Laodicea."

12I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and when I turned I saw seven golden lampstands,

13and among the lampstands one like a son of man, clothed in a robe that reached to His feet, with a golden sash around His chest.

14His head and His hair were white like white wool, like snow, and His eyes were like a flame of fire.

15His feet were like fine bronze glowing as in a furnace, and His voice was like the sound of many waters.

16In His right hand He held seven stars, from His mouth came a sharp two-edged sword, and His face was like the sun shining in its strength.

17When I saw Him, I fell at His feet as though dead. He laid His right hand on me and said, "Do not be afraid. I am the First and the Last,

18and the Living One. I was dead, and I am alive forever and ever, and I hold the keys of death and of Hades.

19So write what you have seen, what is, and what is to take place after this.

20As for the mystery of the seven stars you saw in My right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches."

Notes

  • v1 "what must take place quickly" — en tachei, which can mean soon or swiftly, once it begins; quickly carries both. The book's last chapter repeats the words (22:6). In v3 the time is near.

  • vv4, 8 "Him who is and who was and who is to come" — after apo, from, Greek grammar calls for a different case, but John leaves the title as it stands, ho ōn, the One who is, as if God's name could not be bent to fit the sentence. Ho ōn is the name God gives at the bush in the Greek Old Testament: Egō eimi ho ōn, I am the One who is (Exodus 3:14).

  • v6 "a kingdom, priests to His God" — what God told Israel at Sinai: You will be for Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation (Exodus 19:6).

  • v7 "He is coming with the clouds… those who pierced Him… will mourn" — two prophets in one line: with the clouds of heaven there came one like a son of man (Daniel 7:13), and they will look to Me, whom they have pierced, and they will mourn for him (Zechariah 12:10).

  • v10 "in the Spirit" — en pneumati, with no article: God's Spirit taking hold of John, or John in spirit, carried out of his ordinary senses. English has to choose with the capital letter; the book uses the same words when the vision moves on (4:2; 17:3; 21:10).

  • vv13–14 "one like a son of man… His head and His hair were white like white wool, like snow" — Daniel's words for the one who comes with the clouds (Daniel 7:13), and for the Ancient of Days on the throne: His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head like pure wool (Daniel 7:9). The one like a son of man has the features of the Ancient of Days.

  • v15 "fine bronze… the sound of many waters" — chalkolibanon, a word found in the Greek Bible only in this book (here and 2:18); what metal it names is uncertain. The voice is the voice of God's glory in Ezekiel: His voice was like the sound of many waters (Ezekiel 43:2).

  • v17 "I am the First and the Last" — what the LORD says of Himself in Isaiah: I am the first and I am the last; besides Me there is no god (Isaiah 44:6; 48:12).

  • v20 "the angels of the seven churches" — angeloi, the word for God's heavenly messengers that also means a messenger sent by people. Each of the next seven letters is addressed to the angel of the church; whether these are heavenly beings or the churches' human messengers, the Greek does not say.

chapters.title: To the One Who Overcomes
chapters.html:
Revelation 2

To Ephesus

1"To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: This is what He says, the One who holds the seven stars in His right hand, who walks among the seven golden lampstands:

2I know your works, your toil and your endurance, and that you cannot bear evil people. You have tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and found them false.

3You have endurance, and you have borne up for My name's sake, and have not grown weary.

4But I have this against you: you have left your first love.

5Remember, then, from where you have fallen; repent, and do the first works. If not, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.

6Yet you have this: you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.

7Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.

To Smyrna

8To the angel of the church in Smyrna write: This is what He says, the First and the Last, who was dead and came to life:

9I know your affliction and your poverty (but you are rich), and the slander of those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

10Do not fear what you are about to suffer. The devil is about to throw some of you into prison, so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction for ten days. Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life.

11Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who overcomes will not be harmed by the second death.

To Pergamum

12To the angel of the church in Pergamum write: This is what He says, the One who has the sharp two-edged sword:

13I know where you live, where the throne of Satan is. You hold fast to My name, and you did not deny My faith, even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan lives.

14But I have a few things against you: you have there people who hold to the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, to eat food sacrificed to idols and to commit sexual immorality.

15So you too have some who hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans in the same way.

16Repent, then. If not, I will come to you quickly and make war against them with the sword of My mouth.

17Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who overcomes I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.

To Thyatira

18To the angel of the church in Thyatira write: This is what He says, the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire, and whose feet are like fine bronze:

19I know your works, your love and faith and service and endurance, and that your last works are more than the first.

20But I have this against you: you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and misleads My servants to commit sexual immorality and to eat food sacrificed to idols.

21I gave her time to repent, and she does not want to repent of her immorality.

22I am about to throw her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great affliction, unless they repent of her works.

23I will strike her children dead, and all the churches will know that I am He who searches minds and hearts, and I will give to each of you according to your works.

24But to the rest of you in Thyatira, all who do not hold this teaching and have not known what they call the deep things of Satan, I say: I lay on you no other burden;

25only hold fast what you have until I come.

26The one who overcomes and keeps My works until the end, I will give him authority over the nations,

27and he will shepherd them with a rod of iron, as clay pots are broken in pieces,

28as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star.

29Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

Notes

  • vv1, 8, 12, 18 "This is what He says" — Tade legei, the words the Greek Old Testament uses for This is what the LORD says (Exodus 4:22; Amos 1:6). Each letter opens with them, and each time the speaker is named by something seen in the vision of chapter 1: the stars and the lampstands (1:13, 16), the First and the Last (1:17), the sword (1:16), the eyes and the feet (1:14–15).

  • vv4–5 "your first love… the first works" — first can mean first in time, the love they had at the beginning, or first in place, the love that comes before all else. The Greek allows both, and the English keeps both.

  • v7 "the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God" — the tree in the middle of the garden (Genesis 2:9), whose way the cherubim were set to keep when the human was driven out (Genesis 3:24). Paradise is the Greek Old Testament's word for the garden of Eden.

  • vv7, 11, 17, 26 "the one who overcomes" — ho nikōn, the word of John's first letter: everyone who has been born of God overcomes the world (1 John 5:4). Every letter ends with a promise to the one who overcomes.

  • v13 "Antipas, My witness, My faithful one" — the title Jesus has in 1:5, the faithful witness, given to a man who died for it. Martys, witness, is the word that came to mean a martyr.

  • v14 "the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak" — Moses says the women of Midian, on Balaam's word, led the sons of Israel into unfaithfulness to the LORD in the matter of Peor (Numbers 31:16), when Israel ate the sacrifices of the gods of Moab (Numbers 25:1–2).

  • v23 "I am He who searches minds and hearts" — the LORD's words in Jeremiah: I the LORD search the heart and test the mind, to give to each man according to his ways (Jeremiah 17:10). The Son of God says them of Himself. The Greek has kidneys and hearts, the inmost self.

  • v27 "he will shepherd them with a rod of iron" — Psalm 2:9 as the Greek Old Testament reads it, poimaneis, you will shepherd, where the Hebrew reads You will break them with a rod of iron.

chapters.title: I Stand at the Door and Knock
chapters.html:
Revelation 3

To Sardis

1"To the angel of the church in Sardis write: This is what He says, the One who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works. You have a name for being alive, but you are dead.

2Wake up, and strengthen what remains, which was about to die; for I have not found your works complete before My God.

3Remember, then, what you received and heard; keep it, and repent. If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come upon you.

4Yet you have a few names in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and they will walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

5The one who overcomes will be clothed like them in white garments, and I will never blot his name out of the book of life; I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.

6Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

To Philadelphia

7To the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: This is what He says, the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut, who shuts and no one opens:

8I know your works. I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut. You have little power, and yet you have kept My word and have not denied My name.

9I will make those of the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews and are not, but lie, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and they will know that I have loved you.

10Because you have kept My word about endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of trial that is about to come on the whole world, to try those who live on the earth.

11I am coming quickly. Hold fast what you have, so that no one takes your crown.

12The one who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he will never go out of it again. I will write on him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God, and My own new name.

13Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

To Laodicea

14To the angel of the church in Laodicea write: This is what He says, the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God's creation:

15I know your works: you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot.

16So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of My mouth.

17For you say, 'I am rich; I have prospered, and I need nothing,' and you do not know that you are wretched and pitiable and poor and blind and naked.

18I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire, so that you may be rich, and white garments to clothe yourself, so that the shame of your nakedness may not be seen, and salve to anoint your eyes, so that you may see.

19Those I love, I reprove and discipline. So be zealous, and repent.

20I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and eat with him, and he with Me.

21The one who overcomes, I will give him a place to sit with Me on My throne, as I also overcame and sat down with My Father on His throne.

22Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches."

Notes

  • v5 "I will never blot his name out of the book of life" — Moses' plea at Sinai, blot me out, please, from Your book that You have written, and the LORD's answer, Whoever has sinned against Me, him I will blot out of My book (Exodus 32:32–33).

  • v7 "the key of David, who opens and no one will shut" — the word of Isaiah about Eliakim, steward of the king's house: I will set the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open (Isaiah 22:22).

  • v9 "come and bow down before your feet" — Isaiah's promise to Zion: all who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet (Isaiah 60:14). Here it is turned to a church, and those who bow are those who say they are Jews and are not.

  • v10 "you have kept My word… I also will keep you" — tēreō twice, the one keeping answered by the other.

  • v14 "the Amen, the faithful and true witness" — Isaiah's the God of truth is in Hebrew Elohei amen, the God of Amen (Isaiah 65:16). Jesus takes the word as His name.

  • v14 "the beginning of God's creation" — hē archē tēs ktiseōs. Archē is the beginning of a thing, its first part or its source, and also a ruler; Paul calls Christ the beginning, the firstborn from the dead (Colossians 1:18), and Wisdom says, The LORD got me at the beginning of His way (Proverbs 8:22). Beginning keeps the first two readings open.

  • v19 "Those I love, I reprove and discipline" — Proverbs as the Greek Old Testament has it, whom the Lord loves He reproves (Proverbs 3:12), with the same verb, elenchei.

chapters.title: The Throne in Heaven
chapters.html:
Revelation 4

The One Seated on the Throne

1After this I looked, and a door stood open in heaven, and the first voice I had heard, speaking with me like a trumpet, said, "Come up here, and I will show you what must take place after this."

2At once I was in the Spirit, and a throne stood in heaven, and One was seated on the throne.

3The One seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and around the throne was a rainbow that looked like emerald.

4Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white garments, with golden crowns on their heads.

5From the throne came lightnings and voices and thunders, and before the throne seven torches of fire were burning, which are the seven spirits of God.

6Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, like crystal. In the middle of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.

7The first living creature was like a lion, the second living creature like an ox, the third living creature had a face like a man's, and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle.

8The four living creatures, each of them with six wings, are full of eyes all around and within. Day and night they never rest, saying,

"Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty,
who was and who is and who is to come."

9Whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks to the One seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever,

10the twenty-four elders fall down before the One seated on the throne and worship Him who lives forever and ever, and they cast their crowns before the throne, saying,

11"You are worthy, our Lord and God,
to receive the glory and the honor and the power,
for You created all things,
and by Your will they existed and were created."

Notes

  • vv6–8 "four living creatures… like a lion… an ox… a man… a flying eagle… six wings… Holy, holy, holy" — two visions of the throne in one. Ezekiel saw four living creatures with the face of a human… a lion… an ox… an eagle, and rims full of eyes all around (Ezekiel 1:10, 18); Isaiah saw seraphim, each had six wings, calling Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts (Isaiah 6:2–3). Where Isaiah has the LORD of hosts, the creatures here say the Lord God Almighty, Kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr, the Greek Old Testament's words for the LORD, the God of hosts (Amos 4:13).

  • v5 "lightnings and voices and thunders" — the signs of Sinai, thunders and lightnings, and a heavy cloud on the mountain (Exodus 19:16). Phōnai is both voices and sounds; the book uses it of the trumpet in v1.

  • v8 "who was and who is and who is to come" — the name of 1:4 and 1:8, but with who was first, now that John stands before the throne.

chapters.title: The Lion and the Lamb
chapters.html:
Revelation 5

The Scroll with Seven Seals

1In the right hand of the One seated on the throne I saw a scroll written inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals.

2I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, "Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?"

3No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to look into it.

4I wept and wept, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it.

5One of the elders said to me, "Do not weep. The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome, so that He can open the scroll and its seven seals."

The Lamb

6Then I saw, between the throne and the four living creatures and among the elders, a Lamb standing, as though slain, with seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth.

7He came and took the scroll from the right hand of the One seated on the throne.

8When He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

9They sing a new song, saying,

"You are worthy to take the scroll
and to open its seals,
for You were slain,
and by Your blood You bought for God
people from every tribe and language and people and nation,

10and You have made them a kingdom and priests to our God,
and they reign on the earth."

11Then I looked, and I heard the voice of many angels around the throne and the living creatures and the elders; their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands,

12saying with a loud voice,

"Worthy is the Lamb who was slain
to receive power and wealth and wisdom and might
and honor and glory and blessing!"

13I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and on the sea, and all that is in them, saying,

"To the One seated on the throne and to the Lamb
be blessing and honor and glory and dominion forever and ever!"

14The four living creatures said, "Amen," and the elders fell down and worshiped.

Notes

  • v1 "a scroll written inside and on the back" — Ezekiel's scroll, written on the front and on the back; and written on it were laments and mourning and woe (Ezekiel 2:10).

  • vv5–6 "The Lion of the tribe of Judah… a Lamb standing, as though slain" — the elder announces a lion, and John turns and sees a lamb. A lion's cub is Judah (Genesis 49:9); the root of Jesse… stands as a signal for the peoples (Isaiah 11:10); and the servant goes like a lamb that is led to the slaughter (Isaiah 53:7). Esphagmenon, slain, is the word for an animal killed in sacrifice, and standing says the slain Lamb is alive. The word for overcome is the one promised to the churches in every letter (2:7; 3:21), where Jesus says, as I also overcame.

  • v6 "seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth" — Zechariah's lamp: These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth (Zechariah 4:10).

  • v11 "myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands" — the court of the Ancient of Days: a thousand thousands served Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him (Daniel 7:10).

chapters.title: The Seals Are Opened
chapters.html:
Revelation 6

The Four Horses

1I watched when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures say with a voice like thunder, "Come!"

2I looked, and there was a white horse, and its rider had a bow; a crown was given to him, and he went out overcoming, and to overcome.

3When He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, "Come!"

4Another horse came out, fiery red. Its rider was allowed to take peace from the earth, so that people would slaughter one another, and he was given a great sword.

5When He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, "Come!" I looked, and there was a black horse, and its rider had a pair of scales in his hand.

6I heard what seemed to be a voice among the four living creatures, saying, "A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius; but do not harm the oil and the wine."

7When He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, "Come!"

8I looked, and there was a pale horse, and its rider's name was Death, and Hades followed with him. They were given authority over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword and with famine and with pestilence and by the wild beasts of the earth.

The Souls under the Altar

9When He opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony they held.

10They cried out with a loud voice, "How long, holy and true Master, before You judge and avenge our blood on those who live on the earth?"

11Each of them was given a white robe, and they were told to rest a little longer, until the number was complete of their fellow servants and their brothers who were to be killed as they had been.

The Great Day of Wrath

12I watched when He opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake; the sun became black as sackcloth made of hair, and the whole moon became like blood,

13and the stars of the sky fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind.

14The sky split apart like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place.

15The kings of the earth and the great ones and the commanders, the rich and the strong, and everyone, slave and free, hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains,

16and they say to the mountains and to the rocks, "Fall on us, and hide us from the face of the One seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb;

17for the great day of their wrath has come, and who can stand?"

Notes

  • v2 "he went out overcoming, and to overcome" — nikōn kai hina nikēsē, the verb used of the Lamb, who has overcome (5:5), and of the one who overcomes in every letter. The rider on the white horse is not named. He has been read as Christ, who rides a white horse in 19:11, and as a conqueror, the first of four riders who bring war, famine and death. The text does not say which.

  • vv2–8 the horses, white, red, black and pale — Zechariah's chariots: red horses… black horses… white horses… dappled horses (Zechariah 6:2–3).

  • v6 "A quart of wheat for a denarius" — a choinix, about a quart, a day's bread for one person; a denarius was a day's pay (a denarius for the day, Matthew 20:2). A day's work buys a day's food, and no more.

  • v8 "its rider's name was Death… to kill with sword and with famine and with pestilence" — thanatos, death, is the rider's name and also the word for pestilence, as in the Greek of Ezekiel's four terrible judgments… sword and famine and wild beasts and pestilence (Ezekiel 14:21).

  • v9 "the souls of those who had been slain" — esphagmenōn, the word used of the Lamb, as though slain (5:6).

  • vv12–14 "the moon became like blood… a fig tree drops its unripe figs… like a scroll being rolled up" — the moon to blood, before the great and fearful day of the LORD (Joel 2:31); the skies roll up like a scroll… like a withered fig from the fig tree (Isaiah 34:4).

  • v16 "Fall on us" — the words of Hosea, They will say to the mountains, "Cover us," and to the hills, "Fall on us" (Hosea 10:8).

chapters.title: A Great Multitude No One Could Count
chapters.html:
Revelation 7

The Sealing of the Servants of God

1After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth or on the sea or on any tree.

2I saw another angel coming up from the rising of the sun, with the seal of the living God, and he called out with a loud voice to the four angels who had been given power to harm the earth and the sea,

3saying, "Do not harm the earth or the sea or the trees until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads."

4I heard the number of those who were sealed, a hundred and forty-four thousand, sealed from every tribe of the sons of Israel:

5from the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed, from the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand, from the tribe of Gad twelve thousand,

6from the tribe of Asher twelve thousand, from the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand, from the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand,

7from the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand, from the tribe of Levi twelve thousand, from the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand,

8from the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand, from the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand, from the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed.

Before the Throne and the Lamb

9After this I looked, and there was a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation and tribe and people and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.

10They cry out with a loud voice, saying,

"Salvation belongs to our God, who is seated on the throne, and to the Lamb!"

11All the angels were standing around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and they fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God,

12saying,

"Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might be to our God forever and ever! Amen."

13Then one of the elders answered, saying to me, "These who are clothed in white robes, who are they, and where have they come from?"

14I said to him, "My lord, you know." He said to me, "These are the ones coming out of the great affliction; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.

15That is why they are before the throne of God, and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will pitch His tent over them.

16They will hunger no more, and thirst no more;
the sun will not strike them,
nor any burning heat,

17for the Lamb at the center of the throne will be their shepherd,
and He will guide them to springs of the water of life,
and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes."

Notes

  • v3 "until we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads" — the mark of Ezekiel's vision, when the LORD said, put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the detestable things done in it (Ezekiel 9:4), before the slaughter began.

  • vv5–8 the twelve tribes — the list begins with Judah, the tribe of the Lion (5:5), not with Reuben the firstborn. Dan is not named. Joseph is, and so is his son Manasseh, while Joseph's other son, Ephraim, is not; with Levi counted, the number still comes to twelve.

  • v15 "will pitch His tent over them" — skēnōsei, from skēnē, a tent, the word for the tabernacle. John's Gospel uses the same verb: The Word became flesh and pitched His tent among us (John 1:14).

  • vv16–17 "They will hunger no more… springs of… water… wipe away every tear" — Isaiah's words: They will not hunger or thirst, and neither burning heat nor sun will strike them, for He who has compassion on them will lead them, and by springs of water He will guide them (Isaiah 49:10), and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces (Isaiah 25:8). Here the one who shepherds them is the Lamb.

chapters.title: The Seven Trumpets
chapters.html:
Revelation 8

The Seventh Seal

1When He opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.

2I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.

3Another angel came and stood at the altar with a golden censer, and he was given much incense to offer with the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar before the throne.

4The smoke of the incense rose with the prayers of the saints from the angel's hand before God.

5Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it onto the earth; and there were thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake.

The First Four Trumpets

6The seven angels who had the seven trumpets made ready to blow them.

7The first blew his trumpet, and there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and they were thrown onto the earth. A third of the earth was burned up, a third of the trees were burned up, and all the green grass was burned up.

8The second angel blew his trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea became blood,

9a third of the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.

10The third angel blew his trumpet, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.

11The name of the star is Wormwood. A third of the waters became wormwood, and many people died from the waters, because they had been made bitter.

12The fourth angel blew his trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them were darkened; a third of the day had no light, and so with the night.

13Then I looked, and I heard an eagle flying in midheaven, saying with a loud voice, "Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, at the blasts of the other trumpets that the three angels are about to blow!"

Notes

  • vv3–5 "the prayers of all the saints… filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it onto the earth" — the prayers of the souls under the altar, How long… before You judge (6:10), go up with the incense, and the answer comes down as fire. Ezekiel saw the man in linen told to fill your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city (Ezekiel 10:2).

  • vv7–12 hail and fire, water to blood, darkness — the plagues of Egypt again: fire flashing in the middle of the hail (Exodus 9:24), all the water in the Nile turned to blood (Exodus 7:20), thick darkness in all the land of Egypt (Exodus 10:22). Here each strikes a third.

  • v11 "Wormwood… many people died from the waters, because they had been made bitter" — apsinthos, a bitter plant. Jeremiah's word against a people who had left the law: I am about to feed this people with wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink (Jeremiah 9:15).

chapters.title: The Locusts from the Abyss
chapters.html:
Revelation 9

The Fifth Trumpet

1The fifth angel blew his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and he was given the key to the shaft of the abyss.

2He opened the shaft of the abyss, and smoke rose from the shaft like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke from the shaft.

3Out of the smoke came locusts onto the earth, and they were given power like the power of the scorpions of the earth.

4They were told not to harm the grass of the earth or any green plant or any tree, but only the people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.

5They were not allowed to kill them, but to torment them for five months, and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it stings a man.

6In those days people will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, and death flees from them.

7The locusts looked like horses prepared for battle. On their heads were what looked like crowns of gold, and their faces were like human faces.

8They had hair like women's hair, and their teeth were like lions' teeth.

9They had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots, of many horses rushing into battle.

10They have tails like scorpions, and stingers, and in their tails is their power to harm people for five months.

11They have as king over them the angel of the abyss. His name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.

12The first woe has passed; two woes are still to come after this.

The Sixth Trumpet

13The sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the horns of the golden altar before God,

14saying to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet, "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates."

15The four angels were released, who had been made ready for the hour and day and month and year, to kill a third of mankind.

16The number of the mounted troops was twice ten thousand times ten thousand; I heard their number.

17This is how I saw the horses in the vision, and those who rode them: they had breastplates the color of fire and of hyacinth and of sulfur, and the heads of the horses were like lions' heads, and out of their mouths came fire and smoke and sulfur.

18By these three plagues a third of mankind was killed, by the fire and the smoke and the sulfur coming out of their mouths.

19For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails; their tails are like serpents, with heads, and with them they do harm.

20The rest of mankind, who were not killed by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, so as to stop worshiping demons and idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk;

21nor did they repent of their murders or their sorceries or their sexual immorality or their thefts.

Notes

  • vv7–9 "like horses prepared for battle… teeth like lions' teeth… the sound of chariots" — Joel's locusts: Its appearance is like the appearance of horses… As with the noise of chariots (Joel 2:4–5); its teeth are the teeth of a lion (Joel 1:6).

  • v6 "people will seek death and will not find it" — Job's words of the bitter in soul, who wait for death, and it does not come (Job 3:21).

  • v11 "Abaddon… Apollyon" — Abaddon is the Hebrew word for destruction, from avad, to perish, a name for the place of the dead beside Sheol and Death: Sheol is naked before Him, and Abaddon has no covering (Job 26:6); Abaddon and Death say (Job 28:22). Apollyon is Greek for Destroyer, from apollymi, to destroy. John gives the king of the abyss the name in both languages.

  • vv20–21 "idols of gold and silver and bronze and stone and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk" — Daniel's charge against Belshazzar: You praised the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know (Daniel 5:23).

chapters.html:
Revelation 10

The Angel with the Little Scroll

1I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head; his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire.

2He had a little scroll open in his hand. He set his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land,

3and he cried out with a loud voice, as a lion roars. When he cried out, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.

4When the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, but I heard a voice from heaven say, "Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and do not write it down."

6and swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and what is in it, the earth and what is in it, and the sea and what is in it, that there will be no more time;

8The voice I had heard from heaven spoke to me again, and said, "Go, take the scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land."

  • v6 "there will be no more time" — chronos ouketi estai. Chronos is time, and also the time allowed before something happens; the words can mean that no delay is left, or that time itself comes to an end. No more time carries both, as the Greek does.

chapters.title: The Two Witnesses
chapters.html:
Revelation 11

The Temple Measured

1I was given a reed like a staff, and was told, "Get up and measure the temple of God and the altar, and those who worship there.

2But leave out the court outside the temple; do not measure it, for it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.

The Two Witnesses

3I will give power to My two witnesses, and they will prophesy for twelve hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth."

4These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.

5If anyone wants to harm them, fire comes out of their mouths and devours their enemies; if anyone wants to harm them, this is how he must be killed.

6They have power to shut the sky, so that no rain falls during the days of their prophesying, and they have power over the waters to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague, as often as they wish.

7When they have finished their testimony, the beast that comes up from the abyss will make war on them, overcome them and kill them.

8Their bodies will lie in the street of the great city, which is called, spiritually, Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord also was crucified.

9For three and a half days some from the peoples and tribes and languages and nations look at their bodies, and do not let them be put in a tomb.

10Those who live on the earth rejoice over them and celebrate, and will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who live on the earth.

11But after the three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet, and great fear fell on those who saw them.

12They heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, "Come up here," and they went up to heaven in the cloud, while their enemies watched them.

13At that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. Seven thousand people were killed in the earthquake, and the rest were terrified and gave glory to the God of heaven.

14The second woe has passed; the third woe is coming quickly.

The Seventh Trumpet

15The seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying,

"The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ,
and He will reign forever and ever."

16The twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before God fell on their faces and worshiped God,

17saying,

"We give You thanks, Lord God Almighty,
who is and who was,
for You have taken Your great power
and begun to reign.

18The nations raged, and Your wrath has come,
and the time for the dead to be judged,
and for rewarding Your servants the prophets
and the saints and those who fear Your name, the small and the great,
and for destroying those who destroy the earth."

19Then God's temple in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant was seen in His temple; and there were lightnings and voices and thunders and an earthquake and great hail.

  • v4 "the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth" — Zechariah's lampstand with two olive trees by it, and the angel's answer: These are the two sons of oil who stand by the Lord of all the earth (Zechariah 4:3, 14).

  • vv5–6 "fire comes out of their mouths… power to shut the sky… to turn them into blood" — the signs of Elijah, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word (1 Kings 17:1) and fire came down from heaven and consumed him (2 Kings 1:10), and of Moses, when the Nile turned to blood (Exodus 7:20). The witnesses are not named.

  • v11 "the breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet" — Ezekiel's valley of bones: the breath entered them, and they lived and stood on their feet (Ezekiel 37:10). Pneuma, like the Hebrew ruach there, is breath, wind and spirit.

  • v17 "who is and who was" — the name of 1:4, 1:8 and 4:8 without its last words, who is to come: He has taken His great power and begun to reign.

chapters.title: The Woman and the Dragon
chapters.html:
Revelation 12

The Woman Clothed with the Sun

1A great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.

2She was pregnant, and she cries out in labor, in the pain of giving birth.

3Another sign appeared in heaven: a great red dragon, with seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven diadems.

4His tail sweeps away a third of the stars of heaven, and he threw them to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child.

5She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron; and her child was caught up to God and to His throne.

6The woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there she may be fed for twelve hundred and sixty days.

War in Heaven

7Then war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon. The dragon and his angels fought back,

8but he was not strong enough, and there was no longer any place for them in heaven.

9The great dragon was thrown down, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world; he was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

10Then I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying,

"Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ,
for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down,
who accuses them before our God day and night.

11They have overcome him by the blood of the Lamb
and by the word of their testimony,
for they did not love their lives even to death.

12Therefore rejoice, you heavens,
and you who pitch your tents in them!
Woe to the earth and the sea,
for the devil has come down to you in great fury,
because he knows that his time is short."

The Dragon Pursues the Woman

13When the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.

14The woman was given the two wings of the great eagle, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is fed for a time, and times, and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.

15The serpent poured water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, to sweep her away with the flood.

16But the earth helped the woman: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had poured from his mouth.

17The dragon was enraged with the woman, and went off to make war on the rest of her seed, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus.

Notes

  • v1 "a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and… twelve stars" — Joseph's dream: the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me (Genesis 37:9), which his father read as I and your mother and your brothers (Genesis 37:10). The woman is not named.

  • v5 "a male child, who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron" — Before her pain came upon her, she delivered a male child (Isaiah 66:7), and the king of Psalm 2:9 as the Greek reads it, as at 2:27.

  • vv9, 17 "the ancient serpent… the rest of her seed" — the serpent of the garden, and the word spoken to it: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed (Genesis 3:15).

  • v10 "the accuser of our brothers" — kategōr, the one who brings a charge in court. In Hebrew satan means an accuser, the one who stands at his right hand to accuse him (Zechariah 3:1).

  • v14 "the two wings of the great eagle… a time, and times, and half a time" — what God told Israel at Sinai, I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to Myself (Exodus 19:4); and Daniel's span (Daniel 7:25), the twelve hundred and sixty days of v6 counted another way.

  • v16 "the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river" — as at Korah's rebellion: The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them (Numbers 16:32).

chapters.title: The Two Beasts
chapters.html:
Revelation 13

The Beast from the Sea

1The dragon stood on the sand of the sea. Then I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, with ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten diadems, and on its heads blasphemous names.

2The beast I saw was like a leopard; its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's mouth. The dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority.

3One of its heads seemed to have been slain, to death, but its deadly wound was healed. The whole earth was amazed and followed the beast,

4and they worshiped the dragon, because he had given his authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who can make war against it?"

5The beast was given a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and it was given authority to act for forty-two months.

6It opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His tent, those who pitch their tents in heaven.

7It was allowed to make war on the saints and to overcome them, and it was given authority over every tribe and people and language and nation.

8All who live on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world.

9If anyone has an ear, let him hear.

10If anyone is for captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone is to be killed with the sword, with the sword he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.

The Beast from the Earth

11Then I saw another beast coming up out of the earth. It had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.

12It exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and it makes the earth and those who live on it worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.

13It performs great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to the earth in front of people.

14By the signs it was allowed to perform in the presence of the beast, it deceives those who live on the earth, telling them to make an image for the beast that had the wound of the sword and yet lived.

15It was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast would even speak, and would have those who would not worship the image of the beast killed.

16It makes everyone, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, to be given a mark on their right hand or on their forehead,

17so that no one can buy or sell unless he has the mark, the name of the beast or the number of its name.

18Here is wisdom: let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.

Notes

  • v1 "The dragon stood on the sand of the sea" — the Greek editions number this sentence 12:18; the King James Version, whose numbering this follows, begins chapter 13 with it, and reads I stood. This Greek edition reads he stood, the dragon, and marks the word as a place where manuscripts differ.

  • vv1–2, 5 "ten horns… like a leopard… a bear's… a lion's mouth… a mouth speaking great things" — Daniel's four beasts from the sea, like a lion… like a bear… like a leopard, and the fourth with ten horns, and the little horn with a mouth speaking great things (Daniel 7:4–8). Here the four are one beast.

  • v3 "seemed to have been slain, to death, but its deadly wound was healed" — hōs esphagmenēn, the words used of the Lamb, as though slain (5:6). The beast has its own death and its own return to life.

  • v8 "the book of life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world" — the Greek puts from the foundation of the world after slain: the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world, or names not written from the foundation of the world. In 17:8 the same phrase stands with the names alone, and the Lamb is not in the sentence. The English keeps the Greek order, and both readings.

  • v10 "If anyone is for captivity, into captivity he goes" — Jeremiah's word to the people: those who are for the sword, to the sword… and those who are for captivity, to captivity (Jeremiah 15:2).

  • v18 "it is the number of a man… six hundred and sixty-six" — arithmos anthrōpou: the number of one man, or a human number, a number counted the human way; the same construction in 21:17, metron anthrōpou, is a measure counted the human way. Calculate, psēphisatō, is to count with pebbles. The edition marks the number as a place where manuscripts differ.

chapters.title: The Harvest of the Earth
chapters.html:
Revelation 14

The Lamb on Mount Zion

1Then I looked, and there was the Lamb, standing on Mount Zion, and with Him a hundred and forty-four thousand who had His name and His Father's name written on their foreheads.

2I heard a voice from heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of loud thunder; the voice I heard was like harpists playing on their harps.

3They sing what seems a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders, and no one could learn the song except the hundred and forty-four thousand who had been bought from the earth.

4These are the ones who have not defiled themselves with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were bought from among mankind as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb,

5and in their mouths no lie was found; they are blameless.

The Three Angels

6Then I saw another angel flying in midheaven, with an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who live on the earth, and to every nation and tribe and language and people.

7He said with a loud voice, "Fear God and give Him glory, for the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him who made heaven and earth, the sea and the springs of water."

8Another angel, a second, followed, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who made all the nations drink of the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality."

9Another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a loud voice, "If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives a mark on his forehead or on his hand,

10he too will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, poured out unmixed into the cup of His anger, and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur before the holy angels and before the Lamb.

11The smoke of their torment goes up forever and ever, and they have no rest day or night, those who worship the beast and its image, and whoever receives the mark of its name."

12Here is the endurance of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

13I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on." "Yes," says the Spirit, "so that they may rest from their labors, for their works follow them."

The Harvest and the Winepress

14Then I looked, and there was a white cloud, and seated on the cloud one like a son of man, with a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand.

15Another angel came out of the temple, calling with a loud voice to the One seated on the cloud, "Put in Your sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come, because the harvest of the earth is ripe."

16So the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was reaped.

17Another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle.

18Then another angel came out from the altar, the one who has authority over the fire, and he called with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, "Put in your sharp sickle, and gather the clusters from the vine of the earth, for its grapes are ripe."

19So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered the vintage of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.

20The winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress, as high as the horses' bridles, for sixteen hundred stadia.

Notes

  • v8 "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great" — the cry in Isaiah's vision: Fallen, fallen is Babylon (Isaiah 21:9). The book names the city here for the first time, before it is shown (17–18).

  • vv8, 10 "the wine of the passion… the wine of the wrath of God" — thymos in both: the heat of desire, and the heat of anger. Babylon made the nations drink the one; God gives them the other. Jeremiah was told, Take from My hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it (Jeremiah 25:15).

  • v12 "the faith of Jesus" — tēn pistin Iēsou: the faith they hold in Jesus, or His own faithfulness, which they keep. The Greek does not choose, as at 2:13.

  • vv14–20 the harvest and the winepress — Joel's call: Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full (Joel 3:13); and Isaiah, I have trodden the winepress alone (Isaiah 63:3). One like a son of man on the cloud is the figure of 1:13 and of Daniel 7:13.

  • v20 "sixteen hundred stadia" — a stadion was about 600 feet, so the distance is about 180 miles.

Then I looked, and there was a white cloud, and seated on the cloud one like a son of man, with a golden crown on His head and a sharp sickle in His hand.

So the One seated on the cloud swung His sickle over the earth, and the earth was reaped.
Another angel came out of the temple in heaven, and he too had a sharp sickle.

Then another angel came out from the altar, the one who has authority over the fire, and he called with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, "Put in your sharp sickle, and gather the clusters from the vine of the earth, for its grapes are ripe."
So the angel swung his sickle over the earth and gathered the vintage of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.
The winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress, as high as the horses' bridles, for sixteen hundred stadia.

chapters.html:
Revelation 15

The Song by the Sea of Glass

1Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and wonderful: seven angels with seven plagues, the last, for with them the wrath of God is finished.

2I saw what looked like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who had overcome the beast and its image and the number of its name, standing beside the sea of glass, holding harps of God.

3They sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying,

"Great and wonderful are Your works,
Lord God Almighty;
just and true are Your ways,
King of the ages.

4Who will not fear, Lord,
and glorify Your name?
For You alone are holy.
All the nations will come
and worship before You,
for Your righteous acts have been revealed."

The Seven Bowls

5After this I looked, and the temple of the tent of the Testimony in heaven was opened,

6and out of the temple came the seven angels with the seven plagues, clothed in pure, bright linen, with golden sashes around their chests.

7One of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.

8The temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were finished.

  • vv2–3 "standing beside the sea… the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb" — Israel's song beside the sea after the crossing (Exodus 15), sung now by those who have passed through the beast.   • vv3–4 "King of the ages. Who will not fear, Lord" — Jeremiah's Who would not fear You, King of the nations? (Jeremiah 10:7). The edition reads of the ages and marks the word as a place where manuscripts differ.

  • vv5, 8 "the tent of the Testimony… no one could enter the temple" — the name of the tent in the wilderness, the dwelling, the tent of the Testimony (Numbers 9:15), and its dedication: Moses could not enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of the LORD filled the dwelling (Exodus 40:35).

chapters.title: The Bowls of Wrath
chapters.html:
Revelation 16

The First Five Bowls

1Then I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God on the earth."

2The first went and poured out his bowl on the earth, and foul and painful sores broke out on the people who had the mark of the beast and worshiped its image.

3The second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead man, and every living thing in the sea died.

4The third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of water, and they became blood.

5I heard the angel of the waters say,

"You are just, You who are and who were, the Holy One,
because You have judged these things;

6for they poured out the blood of saints and prophets,
and You have given them blood to drink.
They deserve it."

7I heard the altar say,

"Yes, Lord God Almighty,
true and just are Your judgments."

8The fourth poured out his bowl on the sun, and it was allowed to scorch people with fire.

9People were scorched by the great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues; and they did not repent and give Him glory.

10The fifth poured out his bowl on the throne of the beast, and its kingdom was plunged into darkness. People gnawed their tongues in anguish,

11and they blasphemed the God of heaven for their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.

Armageddon

12The sixth poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, to prepare the way for the kings from the rising of the sun.

13Then I saw, coming out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs.

14They are spirits of demons, performing signs, who go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the battle of the great day of God the Almighty.

15"I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps his garments, so that he will not walk about naked and be seen in his shame."

16They gathered them to the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon.

The Seventh Bowl

17The seventh poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came out of the temple, from the throne, saying, "It is done!"

18There were lightnings and voices and thunders, and a great earthquake, such as there had never been since people have been on the earth, so great was that earthquake.

19The great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. God remembered Babylon the great, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.

20Every island fled away, and the mountains were not found.

21Great hailstones, each as heavy as a talent, fell from heaven on the people, and the people blasphemed God for the plague of the hail, because that plague was exceedingly great.

  • vv2–21 sores, blood, darkness, frogs, hail — the plagues of Egypt a last time: boils, blisters breaking out on man and on beast (Exodus 9:10), the Nile turned to blood (Exodus 7:20), thick darkness (Exodus 10:22), the frog came up and covered the land of Egypt (Exodus 8:6), and the hail (Exodus 9:24). As with Pharaoh, those struck do not repent (vv9, 11).

  • v6 "They deserve it" — axioi eisin, they are worthy, the word sung of the One on the throne and of the Lamb, You are worthy (4:11; 5:9).

  • v15 "I am coming like a thief" — Jesus speaks into the middle of the vision, in the words of the letter to Sardis (3:3), with its white garments (3:4–5, 18).

  • v16 "Armageddon" — read as Hebrew, Har Megiddo, the mountain of Megiddo. chapters.title: Babylon the Great
chapters.html:
Revelation 17

The Woman on the Scarlet Beast

1One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who is seated on many waters,

2with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and with the wine of whose immorality those who live on the earth have become drunk."

3He carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness, and I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast that was full of blasphemous names, with seven heads and ten horns.

4The woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls, and she held in her hand a golden cup full of detestable things and the impurities of her immorality.

5On her forehead was written a name, a mystery: "Babylon the great, the mother of prostitutes and of the detestable things of the earth."

6I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses to Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered greatly.

The Mystery of the Woman and the Beast

7The angel said to me, "Why do you wonder? I will tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carries her, with the seven heads and the ten horns.

8The beast you saw was, and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss and go to destruction. Those who live on the earth, whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, will be amazed when they see the beast, because it was, and is not, and will come.

9This calls for a mind with wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman is seated; they are also seven kings.

10Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain only a little while.

11The beast that was and is not is itself an eighth, and it belongs to the seven, and it goes to destruction.

12The ten horns you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, but they receive authority as kings for one hour, together with the beast.

13These are of one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast.

14They will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for He is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those with Him are called and chosen and faithful."

15He said to me, "The waters you saw, where the prostitute is seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and languages.

16The ten horns you saw, and the beast, will hate the prostitute; they will make her desolate and naked, and they will eat her flesh and burn her up with fire.

17For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose, by being of one mind and giving their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.

18The woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth."

Notes

  • vv1–2, 4 "seated on many waters… a golden cup… drunk" — Jeremiah's words against Babylon: You who live by many waters (Jeremiah 51:13), and Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making all the earth drunk; the nations drank of her wine (Jeremiah 51:7). In v15 the angel says what the waters are.

  • v8 "was, and is not, and will come" — the beast's name is made on the pattern of God's, who was and who is and who is to come (4:8), with is not in the middle. And it goes to destruction, apōleia, the root of Apollyon (9:11).

  • v14 "Lord of lords and King of kings" — the title of God in Moses' words, God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God (Deuteronomy 10:17), given to the Lamb.

chapters.title: Fallen Is Babylon
chapters.html:
Revelation 18

The Fall of Babylon

1After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven, with great authority, and the earth was lit up by his glory.

2He cried out with a mighty voice,

"Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great!
She has become a dwelling place of demons,
a haunt of every unclean spirit,
a haunt of every unclean bird,
a haunt of every unclean and hated beast.

3For all the nations have fallen by the wine of the passion of her immorality,
and the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality with her,
and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury."

4Then I heard another voice from heaven saying,

"Come out of her, My people,
so that you do not share in her sins,
and do not receive her plagues;

5for her sins are heaped up to heaven,
and God has remembered her crimes.

6Pay her back as she herself has paid,
and give her back double for her deeds;
in the cup she mixed, mix her a double portion.

7As much as she glorified herself and lived in luxury,
so much torment and mourning give her.
For in her heart she says,
'I sit as a queen; I am no widow,
and I will never see mourning.'

8That is why her plagues will come in a single day,
death and mourning and famine,
and she will be burned up with fire;
for mighty is the Lord God who has judged her."

The Laments

9The kings of the earth who committed sexual immorality with her and lived in luxury with her will weep and mourn over her when they see the smoke of her burning.

10They will stand far off, for fear of her torment, and say,

"Woe, woe, great city,
Babylon, the mighty city!
For in one hour your judgment has come."

11The merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore:

12cargo of gold and silver, precious stones and pearls, fine linen and purple, silk and scarlet; all kinds of scented wood, all kinds of articles of ivory, all kinds of articles of costly wood and bronze and iron and marble;

13cinnamon and spice, incense and myrrh and frankincense, wine and oil, fine flour and wheat, cattle and sheep, horses and carriages, and bodies, and human souls.

14"The fruit your soul longed for has gone from you, and all your splendor and your glitter are lost to you, never to be found again."

15The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, will stand far off, for fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,

16saying,

"Woe, woe, great city,
clothed in fine linen and purple and scarlet,
adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls!

17For in one hour such great wealth has been laid waste!" Every ship's captain, every passenger, and sailors, and all who work the sea, stood far off

18and cried out as they saw the smoke of her burning, "What city was like the great city?"

19They threw dust on their heads and cried out, weeping and mourning,

"Woe, woe, great city,
where all who had ships at sea grew rich from her wealth!
For in one hour she has been laid waste."

20Rejoice over her, heaven,
and you saints and apostles and prophets,
for God has given judgment for you against her.

The Millstone

21Then a mighty angel picked up a stone like a great millstone and threw it into the sea, saying,

"So with violence will Babylon the great city be thrown down,
and will never be found again.

22The sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters,
will never be heard in you again;
no craftsman of any craft will ever be found in you again;
the sound of the millstone will never be heard in you again;

23the light of a lamp will never shine in you again;
the voice of the bridegroom and the bride will never be heard in you again.
For your merchants were the great ones of the earth,
and all the nations were deceived by your sorcery.

24In her was found the blood of prophets and of saints,
and of all who have been slain on the earth."

Notes

  • v4 "Come out of her, My people" — the word to the exiles in Babylon: Go out from the middle of her, My people! Let each of you save his life from the fierce anger of the LORD! (Jeremiah 51:45).

  • v7 "I sit as a queen; I am no widow, and I will never see mourning" — Babylon's boast in Isaiah: who says in her heart, "I am, and there is none besides me; I will not sit as a widow or know the loss of children" (Isaiah 47:8).

  • vv9–19 the kings, the merchants and the sailors — Ezekiel's lament over Tyre, the city of the sea trade, whose sailors will throw dust on their heads and say, Who is like Tyre? (Ezekiel 27:30, 32).

  • v13 "and bodies, and human souls" — sōmatōn, kai psychas anthrōpōn. Bodies was the market's word for slaves, and the list of cargo ends with them and with human souls. Ezekiel's list of Tyre's trade has human beings and vessels of bronze (Ezekiel 27:13).

  • v21 "a stone like a great millstone… thrown into the sea" — the end of Jeremiah's book against Babylon: tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates, and say, 'So shall Babylon sink and not rise' (Jeremiah 51:63–64).

  • vv22–23 "the sound of the millstone… the light of a lamp… the voice of the bridegroom and the bride" — Jeremiah's sentence on Judah, turned on Babylon: the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp (Jeremiah 25:10).

chapters.title: The Word of God
chapters.html:
Revelation 19

Hallelujah

1After this I heard what sounded like the loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying,

"Hallelujah!
Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,

2for His judgments are true and just.
He has judged the great prostitute
who corrupted the earth with her immorality,
and He has avenged on her the blood of His servants."

3A second time they said,

"Hallelujah!
Her smoke goes up forever and ever."

4The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who is seated on the throne, saying, "Amen. Hallelujah!"

5A voice came from the throne, saying,

"Praise our God,
all you His servants,
you who fear Him, small and great."

The Marriage of the Lamb

6Then I heard what sounded like the voice of a great multitude, like the sound of many waters and like the sound of mighty thunders, saying,

"Hallelujah!
For the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigns.

7Let us rejoice and be glad
and give Him the glory,
for the marriage of the Lamb has come,
and His bride has made herself ready.

8She has been given fine linen, bright and pure, to wear";
for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.

9The angel said to me, "Write: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb." He also said to me, "These are the true words of God."

10I fell at his feet to worship him, but he said to me, "Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."

The Rider on the White Horse

11Then I saw heaven opened, and there was a white horse. Its rider is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war.

12His eyes are like a flame of fire, and on His head are many diadems. He has a name written that no one knows but He Himself.

13He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and the name by which He is called is the Word of God.

14The armies of heaven, clothed in fine linen, white and pure, were following Him on white horses.

15From His mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and He will shepherd them with a rod of iron. He treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty.

16On His robe and on His thigh He has a name written: King of kings and Lord of lords.

17Then I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice to all the birds that fly in midheaven, "Come, gather for the great supper of God,

18to eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of commanders, the flesh of the mighty, the flesh of horses and their riders, and the flesh of all, free and slave, small and great."

19I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered to make war against the rider on the horse and against His army.

20The beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who had performed the signs in its presence, by which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. The two of them were thrown alive into the lake of fire that burns with sulfur.

21The rest were killed by the sword of the rider on the horse, the sword that came out of His mouth, and all the birds gorged themselves on their flesh.

Notes

  • vv1, 3, 4, 6 "Hallelujah" — the Greek spells out the Hebrew hallelu-yah, Praise Yah, the cry that opens and closes the last psalms (Praise Yah!, Psalm 150:1). The book uses it only here, four times, and the voice from the throne says it in Greek, Praise our God (v5).

  • vv11–13 "a white horse… Faithful and True… the Word of God" — the rider is named, as the rider of 6:2 was not: the faithful and true witness of 3:14, and the Word, ho Logos, the name of John 1:1. His other name no one knows but He Himself (v12).

  • vv13, 15 "a robe dipped in blood… He treads the winepress" — Isaiah's warrior coming from Edom in crimsoned garments: I have trodden the winepress alone… I trod them in My anger (Isaiah 63:1, 3). The robe is dipped in blood before the battle begins.

  • vv17–18 "Come, gather for the great supper of God, to eat the flesh of kings" — Ezekiel's call to the birds after the defeat of Gog: Assemble and come; gather from all around to the sacrifice I am making for you… You will eat the flesh of mighty ones (Ezekiel 39:17–18). speech.text: Revelation 19
Hallelujah
After this I heard what sounded like the loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying, "Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,
for His judgments are true and just. He has judged the great prostitute who corrupted the earth with her immorality, and He has avenged on her the blood of His servants."
A second time they said, "Hallelujah! Her smoke goes up forever and ever."
The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who is seated on the throne, saying, "Amen. Hallelujah!"
A voice came from the throne, saying, "Praise our God, all you His servants, you who fear Him, small and great."
The Marriage of the Lamb
Then I heard what sounded like the voice of a great multitude, like the sound of many waters and like the sound of mighty thunders, saying, "Hallelujah! For the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigns.
Let us rejoice and be glad and give Him the glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His bride has made herself ready.
She has been given fine linen, bright and pure, to wear"; for the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.
The angel said to me, "Write: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb." He also said to me, "These are the true words of God."

I fell at his feet to worship him, but he said to me, "Do not do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your brothers who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."

Then I saw heaven opened, and there was a white horse. Its rider is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war.
His eyes are like a flame of fire, and on His head are many diadems. He has a name written that no one knows but He Himself.
He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and the name by which He is called is the Word of God.
The armies of heaven, clothed in fine linen, white and pure, were following Him on white horses.

From His mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations, and He will shepherd them with a rod of iron. He treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty.
